original_value: Deep neural networks have recently been applied to the study of brain disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) with great success. However, the internal logics of these networks are difficult to interpret, especially with regard to how specific network architecture decisions are made. In this paper, we study an interpretable neural network model as a method to identify ASD participants from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data and interpret results of the model in a precise and consistent manner. First, we propose an interpretable fully connected neural network (FCNN) to classify two groups, ASD versus healthy controls (HC), based on input data from resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) between regions of interests (ROIs). The proposed FCNN model is a piecewise linear neural network (PLNN) which uses piecewise linear function LeakyReLU as its activation function. We experimentally compared the FCNN model against widely used classification models including support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and two new classes of deep neural network models in a large dataset containing 871 subjects from ABIDE I database. The results show the proposed FCNN model achieves the highest classification accuracy. Second, we further propose an interpreting method which could explain the trained model precisely with a precise linear formula for each input sample and decision features which contributed most to the classification of ASD versus HC participants in the model. We also discuss the implications of our proposed approach for fMRI data classification and interpretation.

result.paraphrase: Deep neural networks have recently been used with great success to study brain disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD). However, understanding the internal logic of these networks remains difficult, especially when it comes to how specific architectural choices are made. In this paper, we present an interpretable neural network approach for identifying ASD participants from functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data and for explaining the model’s results in a precise, consistent way. First, we introduce an interpretable fully connected neural network (FCNN) to classify two groups, ASD and healthy controls (HC), using input data from resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) between regions of interest (ROIs). The proposed FCNN is a piecewise linear neural network (PLNN) that uses the piecewise linear activation function LeakyReLU. We experimentally evaluated the FCNN against widely used classification methods, including support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and two newly developed classes of deep neural network models, on a large dataset of 871 subjects from the ABIDE I database. The results indicate that the proposed FCNN achieves the highest classification accuracy. Second, we also propose an interpretation method that can explain the trained model precisely with a linear formula for each input sample, as well as the decision features that contributed most to ASD versus HC classification. We further discuss the implications of this approach for fMRI data classification and interpretation.
